statement.p: If C is the line segment from (2,3) to, (0,0), find the value of the line integral:

p.m: \int_C (4 y^2\,\vec i + 4 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =

static.solution:
(0,0) to (2,3) and then take the negative. The line segment is parameterized by x = 2 t\quad y = 3 t, \qquad \mbox{for } 0\le t\le 1.
Then \vec r'(t)=2\vec i+ 3\vec j, so \int_C (4 y^2\,\vec i + 4 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =-\int_0^1\left(36 t^2\,\vec i + 8 t\,\vec j \right)\cdot (2\vec i+3\vec j)\, dt =-\int_0^1(72 t^2 + 24 t)\, dt=-\left(24 t^3 + 12 t^2\right)\bigg|_0^1 = -36.
